Subject: Quantifly inquiry: commit tiers + compliance gating

Hi Ben,

We're evaluating Redwood for a hosted inference tier for our conversational assistant. Procurement and legal want clarity on two things before we can move to a commercial discussion:

1) Per-token pricing and how commit tiers step down at scale (we're looking at anywhere from ~50M to 1B tokens / month depending on PoC results).
2) Whether commit pricing / larger discounts require a signed DPA and SOC2 evidence up front (our security team requires a SOC2 Type II or a recent assurance report before we finalize financial commitments).

Can you send a short pricing band and confirm the gating requirements? If there's a standard DPA you use, please include. Also happy to set a call later this week.

Thanks,
Elena Petrova
Head of Procurement
Quantifly AI

Hi Elena,

Great to hear from you — appreciate the clear ask. Short answers up front: yes, we offer volume-based per-token discounts via commit tiers, and larger / multi-month committed pricing is contingent on a signed DPA and basic SOC2 evidence (SOC2 Type II report or recent SOC2 summary + control questionnaire). That said, for PoCs we can often extend provisional pricing/credits to accelerate evaluation while the paperwork is completed.

High-level pricing bands (hosted text generation):
- No commit (pay-as-you-go): $0.00045 / token
- 50M+ tokens / month commit: $0.00035 / token
- 200M+ tokens / month commit: $0.00027 / token
- 500M+ tokens / month commit: $0.00022 / token

Examples above are illustrative — we can structure stepped tiers (monthly measurement) or an annual committed spend. Discounts and exact breakpoints typically require an account-level contract and DPA.

I'll attach a short SOW and our standard DPA link. Can you share Quantifly's expected token profile (mix of generations vs embeddings, avg sequence length)? That will help tighten the estimate. If it helps, I'm free Friday for a 30-minute call.

Best,
Ben Carter

Folks, forwarding Quantifly's ask. Quick background: target could scale to 200-500M tokens/mo after PoC. Procurement insists on signed DPA + SOC2 evidence before lock-in. They asked whether we can provide provisional pricing while they finalize security docs.

Options I'm considering:
- Offer a 10% provisional discount for a 30-day evaluation window while legal reviews the DPA; require SOC2 summary + commitment to sign DPA within 30 days for deeper tiers.
- Alternatively, hold to policy: require signed DPA and SOC2 summary before offering tiered pricing (slows the deal but cleaner).

Requesting Lauren and Legal/SE input — will legal accept a SOC2 summary + attestation while the full report is provided? Monica, could you comment on technical risk / caching concerns at 200-500M tokens?

Thanks,
Ben

Ben — quick guidance: Legal will not permit full financial commits without a signed DPA. Security can accept a SOC2 summary + bridge attestation (SOC2 readiness) for initial discounts, provided we have a plan and a date to deliver the full Type II report.

Proposal: offer a conditional provisioning discount as follows —
- 30-day evaluation bridge: 10% off listed pay-as-you-go rates (no long-term commitment)
- Conditional commit offer: up to 18% discount on commit tiers (see Ben's bands) if Quantifly signs the DPA and provides SOC2 Type II or an official SOC2 report within 60 days. If SOC2 delivery is delayed beyond 60 days, revert to pay-as-you-go rates and prorated billing adjustments.

Monica — assume runtime and KV cache are fine for initial PoC; quantify costs if they hit sustained 300M tokens / month. Rishi — please prepare a draft price sheet we can send to the customer with conditional language.

- Lauren

Ben — thanks for the clear proposal and the SOC2 summary. A few clarifying items from procurement/legal:

- For measurement, we use billed tokens/month. Can you confirm we can cap measurement to the billing window (i.e., no retroactive adjustments beyond 60 days)?
- Can the 30-day evaluation bridge be extended to 45 days if we demonstrate meaningful progress in PoC?
- Alice (cc) will review the DPA; if we redline, will Redwood accept standard procurement redlines or prefer a short negotiation window?

If we can agree to those points, we'll get the DPA to you and share token profile this afternoon.

Elena
